prompt: Under which conditions does a real gas deviate most from ideal behaviour?
markscheme: **D.** Particles are close together and slow, so particle volume and intermolecular forces matter.

prompt: A fixed mass of gas has volume $V$ at $300\ \text{K}$ and $100\ \text{kPa}$. What is its volume at $600\ \text{K}$ and $400\ \text{kPa}$?

A student finds the molar mass of a volatile liquid. A flask of volume $255\ \text{cm}^3$ is filled with the vapour at $373\ \text{K}$ and $101\ \text{kPa}$. The mass of vapour is $0.580\ \text{g}$.

**(a)** Calculate the molar mass of the liquid. **[3]**

**(b)** Some air remained in the flask, so the vapour did not fill the whole 255 cm³. State and explain the effect on the calculated molar mass. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $n = \tfrac{PV}{RT} = \tfrac{101\times10^3 \times 255\times10^{-6}}{8.31\times373}$ ✓ $= 8.31\times10^{-3}\ \text{mol}$ ✓; $M = \tfrac{0.580}{8.31\times10^{-3}} = 69.8\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ ✓

**(b)** The calculated molar mass is too low ✓; the measured mass of vapour is smaller than for a full flask, but the amount $n$ is calculated from the whole flask volume, so $M = m/n$ is underestimated ✓
